title: echo
description:
An example service that serves one listener and keeps a record in a
PostgreSQL database. Its configuration is the service envelope (probes, log,
drain) and what it needs of its own.

listen.description: The listener the service's own traffic is served on.

postgres.description: The database the service keeps its records in.

keepForever.description: Keep it until somebody deletes it, whatever `days` says.

retention.description:
How long what the service keeps is kept. A default that is a class, which
differs from the class's own in `days`.

labels.description: Labels put on what the service writes. A default that is an open object.

bucket.description:
The bucket. Every install names its own, so the defaults leave it out and the
schema requires it.

prefix.description: What every object's key begins with.

batchSeconds.description: How often a batch is written, in seconds: not more often than every ten.

archive.description: Where the service archives what it served. Absent means it does not.

timeoutSeconds.description: How long one call may take, in seconds.

idempotentOnly.description: Whether a call that is not safe to repeat is repeated too.

proxy.description: A proxy to go through; absent means none.

client.description:
How the service calls out. Every field of it has a default, and so has the
`retry` block inside it, so the whole block may be left out of a document.
